title: Refresh before the request leaves
dek: An expiry check moves ahead of dispatch so the first request after credentials expire can use refreshed credentials.
footer: PR #42 · fix: refresh credentials before dispatch

sections.title: The client already knew how to refresh
sections.content:
The request function in client.ts already checked credential expiry and could refresh the client. Before this change, it sent the payload first, then compared client.expiresAt with the current time. If credentials had expired, it awaited client.refresh() before returning the response.

The missing piece was ordering. Refresh belonged to the request function, but it happened after the operation that needed valid credentials.

sections.title: The first expired request went out too soon
sections.content:
If you made a request just after credentials expired, the old function called client.send(payload) before checking their expiry. The author reports that this first request failed. A refresh after dispatch came too late to help the request already sent.

The correction is to make refresh a prerequisite for dispatch whenever the expiry check requires it. That puts the credential check at the point where it can affect the outgoing request.

sections.title: Check, refresh, then send
sections.content:
The change moves the existing expiry guard to the start of request, ahead of the send. This is now the function's first operation:

{{CODE:0}}

The comparison includes credentials that expire exactly at the current time. When the condition holds, await makes dispatch wait for the refresh to finish. When it does not, execution proceeds directly to the send.

The rest of the function keeps its existing response flow:

{{CODE:1}}

The function still sends the supplied payload and returns the resulting response. The fix changes when it sends, rather than adding a retry after a failed attempt.

The PR body accepts what it calls an extra clock read to avoid the initial failure. The diff shows a narrower change: it moves the existing Date.now() check and adds no second read.

Streaming requests still need a follow-up because, according to the author, they use a separate path. This change covers the request function shown here; the supplied material gives no follow-up issue number or priority.

code.source:
const response = await client.send(payload);
  return response;

sections.title: Make credentials ready before dispatch
sections.content: PR #42 moves the expiry check and awaited refresh ahead of dispatch in client.ts. That addresses the reported first-request failure by refreshing expired credentials before sending the payload, while preserving the response flow. Streaming requests remain a documented follow-up on their separate path.
